implementation_notes: kotlinx.coroutines supplies the pieces: a Channel (bounded via capacity) is the activation queue, one coroutine consuming it runs as the scheduler, and CompletableDeferred or Deferred is the Future handed to callers. State confinement is the documented answer to shared mutable state - a single-threaded dispatcher, limitedParallelism(1), or a Mutex when there is no natural thread - so the servant needs no locks. Prefer suspending servant methods: a blocking call inside a coroutine on Dispatchers.Default starves the pool.
pitfalls: Blocking calls (Thread.sleep, blocking JDBC or file I/O) inside the consumer coroutine pin the dispatcher thread; use withContext(Dispatchers.IO) or suspending APIs.
An unbounded Channel grows without limit; set capacity and let send() suspend for back-pressure.
The consumer coroutine and the channel must be cancelled/closed at shutdown, or the scope leaks and pending senders hang forever.
